description:
Explore the Sundarbans of West Bengal — the world’s largest mangrove forest and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Formed by the confluence of the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers, this tidal estuarine ecosystem showcases rare geomorphological features such as deltaic sedimentation, tidal creek networks, mudflats, saline wetlands, and is home to the iconic Royal Bengal Tiger. More than a biodiversity hotspot, the site offers crucial insights into sea-level change, sediment dynamics, and climate resilience.
